THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -9-  MFA No. 100014 of 2021  C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No.
 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021,
 MFA No. 101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of  2021  JUDGMENT

The claim petitions before the I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Gokak (for short, the 'Trial Court') in ECA.Nos.4, 5, and 6 of 2017 are decided and allowed in part in terms of the order dated 21.10.2020.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Gokak
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Aggrieved by the said judgment, the claimants in each case have filed appeals in MFA Nos.100014,
100012, and 100013 of 2021 and the fourth respondent/insurer before the Trial Court has also filed appeals in MFA Nos.101403, 101404, and 101405 of 2021.
2. The parties to this appeal are referred to as per their rankings before the Trial Court.

3. The liability is fastened on the third and fourth respondents with the liberty to recover the said amount from respondents No.1 and 2.
4.

Brief facts of the case are as under:
- 10 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021,
MFA No. 101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of (i) The accident occurred on 14.10.2016.
The claimants were travelling in a truck bearing registration No.KA-23/A-6988.

(ii) It is stated that the claimants were travelling in the said vehicle as per the instruction of their employer/owner of the truck referred to above, to carry out the Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
8 work of the third respondent who is an electrical contractor.
(iii) The vehicle referred to above toppled and the petitioners in each case before the Trial Court sustained injuries and compensation is claimed against all the respondents.

(iv) In the said claim petitions, the contractor and insurer of the contractor are made parties as third and fourth respondents respectively, and the owner of the vehicle is arrayed as first respondent, and the insurer of the vehicle is arrayed as second respondent.

All the - 11 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of respondents filed objections contesting the matter.

(v) The first respondent/owner of the vehicle filed a statement stating that the claimants are his employees and he took a stand that apart from leasing the vehicle belonging to him, he had also lent the services of the claimants who are his employees to the third respondent/ contractor.
(vi) The third respondent/contractor has denied the relationship of employer and employee between himself and the claimants.

(vii) Fourth respondent/insurer of the contractor has not admitted the liability on the premise that there is no relationship of employer and employee between the third respondent/ contractor and the claimants.

(viii) Second respondent/insured of the vehicle took the stand that the claimants are unauthorized - 12 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of passengers and hence second respondent/insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
5.

As already noticed, the Court has held that the third respondent/contractor and the fourth respondent/insurer of the contractor are jointly and solely liable to pay the compensation with the liberty to recover the said amount from the first and second respondents.
This order is passed on the premise that the third respondent is the principal employer and the first respondent is the contractor.
6. These appeals are admitted to consider the following substantial questions of law:

Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
9
(a) Whether the Trial Court justified in fastening the liability on the third respondent /contractor when the owner of the vehicle made admission regarding employment and payment of salary?

- 13 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of (b) Whether the Trial Court justified in ordering the third respondent/contractor to first pay and then recover from the first and second respondents?

(c) Whether the Trial Court is justified in ignoring the charge sheet which clearly discloses that there was an employer and employee relationship between the claimants and the first respondent/ owner of the vehicle and not the third respondent/ contractor?

7. Sri. Rajesh Rajnal, learned counsel appearing for the insurer of the contractor would submit that the first respondent/owner of the vehicle in his written statement has categorically admitted that the claimants were his employees and that being the position, the Trial Court could not have held that the claimants are the employees of the third respondent contractor.

It is also his contention that all the documents placed before the court particularly the charge sheet produced by the Police would - 14 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of demonstrate that the claimants were employees of the owner of the vehicle and not the employees of the contractor.

He would refer to Section 2(1)(dd)(iii) of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 (for short, the 'Act') and would submit that relationship between the employer and employee can be established even in the absence of any written document to prove the relationship.

When the provision itself provides that there can be employment based on the oral instruction/contract, the Trial Court ought to have taken into consideration the admission of the part of the owner of the vehicle who admitted that the claimants are the employees of the owner of the vehicle.

8. Sri. Santosh S.Hattikatagi, learned counsel for the claimants would submit that the petitions are filed by arraying the contractor as well as the owner of the truck, the insurer of the contractor, and also the insurer of the truck as the parties to the proceedings.

The stand taken in the written statement by the owner of the vehicle is explicit to the fact that the claimants were employed by - 15 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of the owner of the vehicle/first respondent and as such the compensation ought to have been awarded by fixing the liability on the first respondent and second Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
10 respondent/ insurer of respondent No.1.
9.

Sri. Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel appearing for the second respondent/insurer of the vehicle would submit that relationship of employer and employee is not established between the claimants and the owner of the vehicle and the policy of insurance issued by the second respondent in favour of the third respondent/contractor has established the fact that the claimants were employees of the third respondent and the Trial Court is justified in fastening the liability on the contractor and the insurer of the contractor.
10. This Court has perused the impugned judgment and award.
This Court has considered the contentions raised at the Bar.
Issuance of the policy by the second respondent/insurer of the vehicle and the fourth respondent/insurer of the contractor is not in dispute.

Based on the pleadings and evidence placed on record, the Court has concluded that the relationship of employer and employee is not established between the third respondent/contractor and the claimants.
At the same time, the Trial Court has held that the relationship between the claimants and the owner of the vehicle is established.
This finding is not questioned by the owner of the vehicle or the insurer of the vehicle.

However, in the operative portion of the judgment, the Court has held that the third and fourth respondents are liable to pay the compensation with the liberty to recover the said amount from the first and second respondents.

12. As already noticed that the finding of the Court relating to the relationship of employer and employee between the owner of the vehicle and the claimants is not questioned by the insurer of the vehicle as well as the - 17 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of owner of the vehicle.
Thus, the said finding has attained finality.
This finding is based on the written statement filed by the owner of the vehicle and also the evidence led by the owner of the vehicle which is accepted by the Court.

Since there is no challenge in the said finding, this Court is of the view that the Trial Court has erred in fastening the liability on the third and fourth respondents with the liberty to recover the same from the first and second respondents.

Since the relationship of employer and employee is not established between the claimants and the third respondent/contractor, the Trial Court could not have fastened the liability on the third and fourth respondents.
Accordingly, to that said extent, the impugned judgment and awards are set aside.
Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti

on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
11 13.

Sri. Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel appearing for the second respondent/insurer of the vehicle submits that vehicle had a capacity of two persons i.e. one person including the driver, and four persons were travelling in the vehicle and that being the position, there - 18 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of is a violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and the second respondent/insurer of the vehicle should not be held liable to pay the compensation.

As far as this contention is concerned, learned counsel for the claimants would submit that as per Rule 100 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, if the weight of the vehicle is more than 990 kgs. and if the vehicle is a light transport goods vehicle, 3 persons excluding the driver are permitted to travel in the vehicle.
14.
The records would reveal that the unladen weight of the vehicle is 1,650 kgs. and the laden weight is 2,818 kgs.
So this vehicle falls under the sub Rule (ii) of Rule (1) of Rule 100 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules,1989.

entities.text: sub Rule (ii) of Rule (1) of Rule 100
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: For the aforesaid reasons, this Court is of the view that since three persons were travelling in the light transport goods vehicle in question, which had an unladen weight of 1,650 kgs., the claimants who were travelling in the vehicle were not unauthorized passengers.

Accordingly, the second respondent/insurer of the vehicle - 19 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, the substantial questions of the law referred to above have been answered in favour of respondent No.4/insurer of the contractor.

15. As far as the appeals filed by the claimants are concerned, learned counsel for the claimants/appellants would submit that the doctor has assessed 50% disability and Trial Court has not taken into consideration while calculating the loss of income.

The tribunal erred in taking 12%
as the percentage of disability to calculate the loss of future income.

Learned counsel, would refer to Explanation-II of Section 4 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923, and would submit that the percentage of disability assessed by the doctor has to be taken as the basis for calculating disability without any deduction in the percentage of disability assessed by the doctor.

Sri. Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/insurer of the vehicle submits that under Explanation-II of Section 4 of the Act, the percentage of disability to the earning capacity of the employee has to be assessed by the doctor.

However, the doctor who issued the Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
12 disability certificate has not given any evidence relating to the functional disability.
The Trial Court is thus justified in not accepting the claim of the claimants relating to the alleged 50% disability as the basis to determine the loss of future income.
17. This Court has perused the said provision and also the record.

Explanation-II of Section 4 of the Act reads as under:
"In assessing the loss of earning capacity for the purpose of sub-clause (ii), the qualifying medical practitioner shall have due regard to the percentages of loss of earning capacity in relation to different injuries specified in Schedule-I"
- 21 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of 18.
On reading the aforementioned Explanation-II, it is explicit that the doctor must have due regard to the loss of earning capacity while issuing a disability certificate.
In other words, the doctor is under obligation to assess the loss of earning capacity of the insured with reference to the injuries sustained.
The evidence led by the doctor and also the disability certificate issued by the doctor do not refer to the functional disability with reference to the loss of earning capacity.
It only refers to the disability of the particular limb.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of the view that Sri.
Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel appearing for the insurer is justified in opposing the claim of the claimants for enhancement of compensation.
19.
This Court finds that contentions relating to the enhancement of compensation in these cases do not give rise to any substantial questions of law.

Accordingly, appeals filed by the claimants are disposed of modifying - 22 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of the portion of the judgment and award in respect of the liability as already discussed above.
20.
The appeals filed by the fourth respondent/insurer of the contractor are allowed as already discussed above.
21. The amount in deposit by the fourth respondent/insurer of the contractor, if any, shall be released in favour of the insurer.
22. The second respondent/insurer of the vehicle shall deposit the amount determined by the trial Court, within six weeks from the date of the receipt of a certified copy of this order.

Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
13 23.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No.100014/2021, MFA No.100012/2021 MFA No.100013/2021 are allowed in part fastening the liability to pay the compensation - 23 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of on the second respondent/United India Insurance Company.
(ii) MFA No.10143/2021, MFA No.101404/2021, and MFA No.101405/2021 are allowed.

The liability to pay the compensation determined by the trial Court is fastened on the third respondent/
United India Insurance Company.

opennyai_summary.issue:
6. These appeals are admitted to consider the following substantial questions of law:
(a) Whether the Trial Court justified in fastening the liability on the third respondent /contractor when the owner of the vehicle made admission regarding employment and payment of salary?
- 13 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of (b) Whether the Trial Court justified in ordering the third respondent/contractor to first pay and then recover from the first and second respondents?
(c) Whether the Trial Court is justified in ignoring the charge sheet which clearly discloses that there was an employer and employee relationship between the claimants and the first respondent/ owner of the vehicle and not the third respondent/ contractor?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
When the provision itself provides that there can be employment based on the oral instruction/contract, the Trial Court ought to have taken into consideration the admission of the part of the owner of the vehicle who admitted that the claimants are the employees of the owner of the vehicle.
The stand taken in the written statement by the owner of the vehicle is explicit to the fact that the claimants were employed by - 15 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of the owner of the vehicle/first respondent and as such the compensation ought to have been awarded by fixing the liability on the first respondent and second Shri.Yallappa S/O Mallappa Mudhol vs Shri.Mallappa S/O Gangappa Yaragatti on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199249615/
10 respondent/ insurer of respondent No.1.
9.
As far as this contention is concerned, learned counsel for the claimants would submit that as per Rule 100 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, if the weight of the vehicle is more than 990 kgs. and if the vehicle is a light transport goods vehicle, 3 persons excluding the driver are permitted to travel in the vehicle.
14.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
At the same time, the Trial Court has held that the relationship between the claimants and the owner of the vehicle is established.
Thus, the said finding has attained finality.
Since there is no challenge in the said finding, this Court is of the view that the Trial Court has erred in fastening the liability on the third and fourth respondents with the liberty to recover the same from the first and second respondents.
Since the relationship of employer and employee is not established between the claimants and the third respondent/contractor, the Trial Court could not have fastened the liability on the third and fourth respondents.
So this vehicle falls under the sub Rule (ii) of Rule (1) of Rule 100 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules,1989.
For the aforesaid reasons, this Court is of the view that since three persons were travelling in the light transport goods vehicle in question, which had an unladen weight of 1,650 kgs., the claimants who were travelling in the vehicle were not unauthorized passengers.
Accordingly, the second respondent/insurer of the vehicle - 19 - C/W MFA No. 100012 of 2021, MFA No. 100013 of 2021, MFA No. 101403 of 2021, MFA No.
101404 of 2021, MFA No. 101405 of is liable to pay the compensation.
The tribunal erred in taking 12%
as the percentage of disability to calculate the loss of future income.
The Trial Court is thus justified in not accepting the claim of the claimants relating to the alleged 50% disability as the basis to determine the loss of future income.
On reading the aforementioned Explanation-II, it is explicit that the doctor must have due regard to the loss of earning capacity while issuing a disability certificate.
In other words, the doctor is under obligation to assess the loss of earning capacity of the insured with reference to the injuries sustained.
The evidence led by the doctor and also the disability certificate issued by the doctor do not refer to the functional disability with reference to the loss of earning capacity.
It only refers to the disability of the particular limb.
Under these circumstances, this Court is of the view that Sri.
Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel appearing for the insurer is justified in opposing the claim of the claimants for enhancement of compensation.
